title: 2015 AMC 10A Problem 20
statement: A rectangle with positive integer side lengths in \(\mathrm{cm}\) has area \(A\) \(\mathrm{cm}^2\) and perimeter \(P\) \(\mathrm{cm}.\) Which of the following numbers cannot equal \(A+P?\)

solutions.text:
Let the side lengths be positive integers \(x\) and \(y\). Then \[ \begin{aligned} &A+P=xy+2x+2y \\ &=(x+2)(y+2)-4. \end{aligned} \] Hence \(A+P+4\) must factor into two integers both at least \(3\).

The answer choices plus \(4\) are \(104,106,108,110,112\). All except \(106\) have a factorization with both factors at least \(3\): \[104=4\cdot26,\] \[108=9\cdot12,\] \[110=10\cdot11,\] \[112=7\cdot16.\] But \(106=2\cdot53\), so it cannot equal \((x+2)(y+2)\).

Thus, B is the correct answer.
